name: Faster and more efficient generation
gist: Papers on speeding up generation while keeping quality high, including distillation (learning from larger models), few-step sampling, and compression techniques.
explain: Faster and more efficient generation means reducing both time and computational resources because standard generative models need many steps (often 50-1000) to go from noise to a real output, and each step is computationally expensive. Generative models face a core tradeoff: quality versus speed. Most models can produce beautiful output, but often very slowly, making them impractical for real work. A beautiful image that takes 30 seconds to generate is not useful for interactive applications because users want real-time feedback and iteration. Neither is a video that takes an hour, because video production already consumes time and waiting additional hours for generation makes it impractical. Efficient generation is a practical necessity—it's the difference between a research demo and something millions of people can use. The research question is: can we get good quality in fewer steps, so users get outputs in seconds rather than minutes?

There are several approaches. Distillation means training a small, fast 'student' model to mimic a large, slow 'teacher' model. The student learns to do in 5 steps what the teacher does in 50 steps. Few-step sampling means rethinking the mathematics so that you can jump multiple noise-removal steps at once—instead of removing 1% of noise 100 times, can you remove 10% of noise 10 times? Quantization compresses the model itself—storing numbers with lower precision—so it runs faster and uses less memory. Pruning removes parts of the model that don't contribute much. Caching means remembering intermediate computations rather than redoing them.

The research here is a mix of mathematical work (proving you can use bigger steps while still converging to good outputs) and systems work (engineering models to be fast without sacrificing quality). A key insight is that there's often a tradeoff curve: you can be very fast but lower quality, or slower but higher quality. Papers here explore where that curve lies for different methods and how to push it forward. The practical impact is huge because faster generation means more interactive applications (you can iterate in real time), lower energy use (the system spends less time computing, which matters both for cost and for the environment), and accessibility on lower-end devices like phones (a model that needs a data center is only useful for large organizations with big budgets, while a model that runs on a phone is useful for everyone).

papers.title: Decoupled DMD: CFG Augmentation as the Spear, Distribution Matching as the Shield
papers.contribution: Decoupled understanding enables principled modifications like decoupling noise schedules for engine and regularizer, leading to improved performance.

papers.title: Flow Straight and Fast in Hilbert Space: Functional Rectified Flow
papers.contribution: Removes restrictive measure-theoretic assumptions in existing functional flow matching theory and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing functional generative models.

papers.title: Generalised Flow Maps for Few-Step Generative Modelling on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.contribution: GFMs achieve state-of-the-art sample quality and log-likelihood on geospatial, RNA, and hyperbolic data with single/few-step evaluation.

papers.title: Optimizing Few-Step Generation with Adaptive Matching Distillation
papers.contribution: Improves SDXL HPSv2 score from 30.64 to 31.25 and enhances training robustness; outperforms state-of-the-art on image and video generation.

papers.title: PairFlow: Closed-Form Source-Target Coupling for Few-Step Generation in Discrete Flow Models
papers.contribution: Matches or surpasses two-stage finetuning performance with only 1.7% training compute overhead.

papers.title: Soft-Di[M]O: Improved one-step Image Discrete Model
papers.contribution: Soft-DiMO achieves one-step FID of 1.56 on ImageNet-256 with GAN refinement, improving GenEval and HPS scores on text-to-image with reward fine-tuning.

papers.title: Universal Inverse Distillation for Matching Models with Real-Data Supervision (No GANs)
papers.contribution: Unified theoretical foundation extends previous distillation methods and enables practical real-data-supervised training across different generative frameworks.

papers.title: pi-Flow: Policy-Based Few-Step Generation via Imitation Distillation
papers.contribution: On ImageNet 256×256, π-Flow achieves 1-NFE FID of 2.85 outperforming previous 1-NFE models; on FLUX.1-12B and Qwen-Image-20B at 4 NFEs achieves substantially better diversity than state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Any2Any: Unified Arbitrary Modality Translation for Remote Sensing
papers.contribution: Outperforms pairwise translation across 14 tasks with strong zero-shot generalization to unseen modality combinations; introduces RST-1M million-scale remote sensing dataset.

papers.title: BézierFlow: Learning Bézier Stochastic Interpolant Schedulers for Few-Step Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves 2-3x performance improvement for sampling with ≤10 NFEs in only 15 minutes of training, consistently outperforming timestep-learning methods.

papers.title: Categorical Flow Maps
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art few-step results on images, molecular graphs, and text with strong single-step generation performance.

papers.title: CoD-Lite: Real-Time Diffusion-Based Generative Image Compression
papers.contribution: Achieves real-time 60 FPS encoding and 42 FPS decoding with 85% bitrate reduction compared to MS-ILLM.

papers.title: Consistent Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: Together, these results position CDLM as a principled and scalable foundation for the ne.

papers.title: Decoupled MeanFlow: Turning Flow Models into Flow Maps for Accelerated Sampling
papers.contribution: Achieves 1-step FID of 2.16 on ImageNet 256x256 and 4-step FID of 1.51, delivering 125x faster inference than standard flow models.

papers.title: DeepWeightFlow: Re-Basined Flow Matching for Generating Neural Network Weights
papers.contribution: Generates ensembles of hundreds of networks in minutes without finetuning, scaling to large architectures with better transfer learning performance than diffusion methods.

papers.title: Distillation Models are Good Samplers for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Reduces rollout cost by an order of magnitude while improving OCR and GenEval performance on text-to-image and text-to-video generation.

papers.title: Diversity-Preserved Distribution Matching Distillation for Fast Visual Synthesis
papers.contribution: Preserves sample diversity while maintaining competitive visual quality without perceptual or adversarial regularization.

papers.title: Eliminating VAE for Fast and High-Resolution Generative Detail Restoration
papers.contribution: GenDR-Pix achieves 2.8× acceleration and 60% memory-saving compared to GenDR with negligible visual degradation and can restore 4K images.

papers.title: FACM: Flow-Anchored Consistency Models
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art FID of 1.32 with two steps and 1.70 with just one step on ImageNet 256×256.

papers.title: Finite-Time Convergence Analysis of ODE-based Generative Models for Stochastic Interpolants
papers.contribution: Yields improved theoretical guarantees for diffusion models in terms of smoothness requirements and dimensional dependence; numerical experiments validate error bounds and complexity analyses.

papers.title: Free Lunch for Stabilizing Rectified Flow Inversion
papers.contribution: Significantly improves inversion stability, image reconstruction quality, and editing fidelity on PIE-Bench while reducing neural function evaluations.

papers.title: FutureFill: Fast Generation from Convolutional Sequence Models
papers.contribution: Requires prefill cache growing only with tokens to generate and demonstrates substantial efficiency gains on language modeling.

papers.title: GAS: Improving Discretization of Diffusion ODEs via Generalized Adversarial Solver
papers.contribution: The method shows superior performance compared to existing solver training methods under similar resource constraints.

papers.title: GEM: Geometric Erasure by Contrastive Velocity Matching in Rectified Flows
papers.contribution: Effectively suppresses unwanted concepts while preserving benign generation in Rectified Flow models through the unified geometric guidance framework.

papers.title: Generative Modeling from Black-Box Corruptions via Self-Consistent Stochastic Interpolants
papers.contribution: Achieves theoretically grounded generative modeling from corrupted data with superior performance on natural image and scientific reconstruction tasks.

papers.title: IDLM: Inverse-distilled Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: IDLM reduces inference steps 4×-64× while preserving generation quality across multiple DLMs.

papers.title: Joint Geometric and Trajectory Consistency Learning for One-Step Real-World Super-Resolution
papers.contribution: Delivers superior performance over representative baselines while maintaining minimal latency, addressing both consistency drift and geometric decoupling in one-step super-resolution.

papers.title: Large Scale Diffusion Distillation via Score-Regularized Continuous-Time Consistency
papers.contribution: Scales to 14B models and 5-second videos, matches state-of-the-art DMD2 on quality while mitigating mode collapse and improving diversity without GAN tuning.

papers.title: Latent Stochastic Interpolants
papers.contribution: LSI learns effective latent representations while sidesteppping simple priors of diffusion models and computational demands of high-dimensional SI.

papers.title: LoRAGen: Structure-Aware Weight Space Learning for LoRA Generation
papers.contribution: LoRAGen achieves 96.0% performance on FLAN-T5-large and 72.7% on Gemma-2-2B-Instruct in-distribution, and 40.2% zero-shot on unseen tasks.

papers.title: M-Star: Markovian Projection of Star-Shaped Diffusion for Exponential Family Distributions
papers.contribution: Enables few-step or single-step generation while maintaining flexibility across multiple generative tasks.

papers.title: Mean Flow Distillation: Robust and Stable Distillation for Flow Matching Models
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on high-dimensional manifolds including 4D occupancy forecasting and text-to-image generation, enabling high-fidelity single-step generation.

papers.title: Measurement-Consistent Langevin Corrector for Stabilizing Latent Diffusion Inverse Problem Solvers
papers.contribution: Stabilizes LDM-based solvers without relying on linear manifold assumptions that often fail in latent space.

papers.title: One-Step Flow for Image Super-Resolution with Tunable Fidelity-Realism Trade-offs
papers.contribution: OFTSR achieves state-of-the-art one-step super-resolution with tunable fidelity-realism trade-off on FFHQ/DIV2K/ImageNet.

papers.title: Overclocking Electrostatic Generative Models
papers.contribution: Distilled generators achieve near-teacher or superior sample quality using only few function evaluations, with faster convergence at finite auxiliary dimensionality.

papers.title: PODiff: Latent Diffusion in Proper Orthogonal Decomposition Space for Scientific Super-Resolution
papers.contribution: Achieves comparable reconstruction accuracy to pixel-space diffusion with substantially smaller latent space, less memory, and more reliable uncertainty vs. deterministic/MC Dropout baselines.

papers.title: Primal-Spectral Generative Modeling: Fast Analytical Generation via Pseudoinverse Lévy Inversion
papers.contribution: For ImageNet $256 \times 256$, 1-NFE PiLI achieves a competitive FID of **1.66** using only **26** Gflops, representing a **170$\times$** reduction in total Gflops compared to the 4,436 Gflops required by the 25-NFE DPM-Solver++..

papers.title: Scaling Sequence-to-Sequence Generative Neural Rendering
papers.contribution: Sets state-of-the-art on view synthesis benchmarks, matching per-scene optimization in many-view settings and substantially outperforming in few-view zero-shot settings.

papers.title: Shortcut Diffusion Training with Cumulative Consistency Loss: An Optimal Control View
papers.contribution: The approach significantly improves one-step and few-step generation quality compared to self-consistency loss baselines under the same training budget.

papers.title: SlerpFlow: Spherical Trajectory Correction for Rectified Flow Inversion
papers.contribution: Achieves high-precision inversion while maintaining computational efficiency of first-order Euler solver without requiring additional training.

papers.title: SpeechOp: Inference-Time Task Composition for Generative Speech Processing
papers.contribution: SpeechOp achieves state-of-the-art content preservation and improves core TTS performance through multi-task learning and inference-time task composition.

papers.title: StreamFlow: Theory, Algorithm, and Implementation for High-Efficiency Rectified Flow Generation
papers.contribution: Accelerates 512x512 image generation speed up to 611%, far exceeding the 18% achieved by existing public methods through non-generalized acceleration.

papers.title: StyleDistillation: A New Insight of Image Style Enables Personalized Aesthetic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Achieves outstanding style reproduction and prompt alignment with support for style editing and fusion operations.

papers.title: Tilt Matching for Scalable Sampling and Fine-Tuning
papers.contribution: Tilt Matching achieves state-of-the-art sampling efficiency on Lennard-Jones systems and competitive fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion without reward multipliers or backprop through trajectories.

papers.title: TwinFlow: Realizing One-step Generation on Large Models with Self-adversarial Flows
papers.contribution: Achieves GenEval 0.83 at 1-NFE outperforming distillation baselines; scales to 20B multi-modal model with efficient few-step generation.

papers.title: VecDesigner: Exploring Visual Guidance and Structural Consistency for Semantic Typography
papers.contribution: Outperforms existing methods in semantic expression and structural preservation, generating high-quality, expressive, and legible semantic glyphs.

papers.title: XYZFlow: Scaling Multidimensional Shortcut Flows for Efficient Generative Modeling
papers.contribution: XYZFlow achieves 7.2-8.5x teacher speedups with competitive FID, delivering superior quality-latency trade-offs.

papers.title: Zero-Flow Encoders
papers.contribution: Demonstrate zero-flow encoders' effectiveness on learning latent representations and certifying conditional independence for both synthetic and real-world datasets.
